- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates downside; add 3–5% buffer to downward revisions.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to dampen overshoots.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility or alternating extremes, forecast should be anchored closer to recent 7-day average rather than 30-day trend.
- For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30d), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust by applying 1–2% downward correction if price exceeds 2σ above recent mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to drift toward historical mean; use sentiment-weighted moving average to anchor forecast.
